$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Cloud KMS. See s3.json for the contract. Feature ids share one namespace with AWS; GCP ids start with 'gcp.'.

gcp.kms.keyring.crud.title: Key rings (create, get, list across locations)

gcp.kms.key.rotation.title: Key rotation (rotation period + manual Rotate key)
limitations: The rotation period and next rotation time are stored and returned exactly as configured, but Vyomi has no background scheduler — it never rotates a key on its own; use "Rotate key" or wait for an external caller to do it.

gcp.kms.key.versions.title: Key versions (create, make primary, enable, disable, destroy, restore)

gcp.kms.key.permissions.title: Permissions (IAM policy on a key)
limitations: setIamPolicy, :encrypt and :decrypt are enforced against the policy's bindings (an ungranted caller gets PERMISSION_DENIED; a caller with the matching predefined role — cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter/Encrypter/Decrypter/Viewer/admin — is let through). getIamPolicy and the key/version CRUD calls stay open to any caller, and conditions, custom roles, and org-policy constraints are not evaluated.

gcp.kms.inventory.title: Key inventory (project-wide key search across all key rings and locations)

gcp.kms.autokey.title: Autokey (automatic per-resource key ring/key provisioning)
limitations: AutokeyConfig (enable + key project) and CreateKeyHandle are real and enforced: a KeyHandle can only be created once Autokey is ACTIVE for the project, and creating one really provisions an "autokey-{location}" key ring and a brand-new CryptoKey (own key material) in the configured key project — not a stored reference.

The real API configures Autokey on a folder/organization and derives each project's effective config from its ancestry; Vyomi models projects only (no folder/org hierarchy — see core/gcp_resourcemanager_core.py), so AutokeyConfig is a project-scoped singleton instead.

Other Vyomi services' create flows (Compute disks, Cloud SQL instances, …) don't yet call CreateKeyHandle automatically when a CMEK option is chosen; provision the key handle explicitly via this page or the API first.
